title: Two nights of utility work at Broadway–City Hall
summary: Broadway Subway crews scheduled pipe work beside the Canada Line station from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. on two nights starting August 30.

title: Passengers take their first trips on the Evergreen Extension
summary: Millennium Line trains began serving the new stretch from Lougheed Town Centre to Lafarge Lake–Douglas.

title: Ottawa and B.C. fund the Broadway Subway
summary: The two governments announced construction funding for six Millennium Line stations between VCC–Clark and Arbutus.

title: Port Coquitlam considers a Millennium Line branch
summary: Mayor Brad West described a possible branch near Coquitlam Central. The city had yet to choose station sites.

title: Major construction begins on the Broadway Subway
summary: With utilities moved and sites prepared, B.C. announced the start of major work on the Millennium Line extension to Arbutus.

title: North Shore study compares routes to Waterfront and Metrotown
summary: The study tested two SkyTrain options from Park Royal: Gold to Waterfront and Purple to Metrotown. The choice of technology remained open.

title: Mayors’ Council backs a route from Arbutus to UBC
summary: On April 22, the council endorsed four station areas: Macdonald, Alma, Jericho and the UBC trolley bus loop. It left funding and the choice of elevated or underground track for later.

title: B.C. approves funding for SkyTrain to Langley
summary: The province released the business case and confirmed funding for the Expo Line extension from King George to Langley City Centre.

title: Vancouver keeps two Cambie Street stations in its plan
summary: City planning reports identify West 33rd and West 57th avenues as possible Canada Line stops. Construction funding was still outstanding.

title: Capstan Station opens in Richmond
summary: Canada Line trains on the Richmond branch began stopping at Capstan, between Bridgeport and Aberdeen.

title: First guideway columns stand along Fraser Highway
summary: By February, columns were visible at several sites. B.C. put the start of major construction in November 2024.

title: Port Coquitlam and TransLink work on a SkyTrain business plan
summary: Port Coquitlam described the work in its 2025 annual report. Station sites and construction funding were still open questions.

title: Construction reaches all eight Surrey–Langley stations
summary: Crews had finished six foundations. Foundation work continued at 152 Street and had just begun at Willowbrook. At Fleetwood and Green Timbers, the station structures had risen above ground.

title: First test trains run on the Broadway Subway
summary: Testing began near VCC–Clark. Drivers were checking how trains, track and signals worked together before testing automatic train control.

title: Traffic to shift on Broadway at Oak Street
summary: Crews planned to inspect sewer lines overnight on August 23. On August 27, traffic was due to move to the south side of Broadway so crews could remove the temporary deck on the north side.

title: Gravel trucks to use East 1st Avenue
summary: Trucks were due between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. to deliver gravel for the space above the Great Northern Way–Emily Carr station roof.

title: Fall work schedule for the Surrey–Langley extension
summary: The September advisory lists where crews planned to lay rails, assemble the elevated trackway and build the stations through November.

title: Expo Line extension to Langley named for Dave Barrett
summary: B.C. named the extension after former premier Dave Barrett. It will carry Expo Line trains from King George to Langley City Centre.

title: Broadway Subway crews near the end of track installation
summary: B.C. expected crews to lay the last track that week. They had already removed the temporary road deck at Broadway–City Hall in August.

title: Langley Launcher reaches Langley City Centre
summary: The machine that lifts sections of elevated track into place reached the eastern end of the extension. B.C. put guideway construction at about 65% complete.

title: 5:30 a.m. start for concrete work at Fleetwood
summary: Crews at Fraser Highway and 160 Street scheduled a continuous pour for October 9, with work allowed until midnight.

title: Two long concrete shifts at 152 Street
summary: At the future station on Fraser Highway, crews scheduled concrete work from 5 a.m. to midnight on October 20 and 21.

title: Traffic to move north on Broadway at South Granville
summary: The October 22 shift between Granville and Hemlock would give crews room to remove the temporary road deck. Inside the station, workers were finishing ceilings and tile and testing equipment.

title: Sunday shifts at Bakerview and Hillcrest
summary: Crews planned to install reinforcing steel and pour concrete at both stations on Sundays from October 25 through November 8, between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m.

title: Last road deck panels to come out at Arbutus
summary: Traffic between Arbutus and Cypress was due to move to the north side of Broadway on November 2. Crews could then take out the panels and girders on the south side.

title: Overnight work planned for the Oak–VGH water main
summary: Crews expected to spend about four nights preparing the connection, starting as early as October 25. Road repairs continued on the north side of Broadway.

title: Overnight pipe work on Hemlock Street
summary: Crews planned to locate buried utilities on October 29 before installing new pipes. Work to fill the excavation and rebuild Broadway continued nearby.

title: Concrete work at Hillcrest to run until midnight
summary: Crews at Fraser Highway and 184 Street planned a 5 a.m. start on November 3 so they could pour concrete continuously.

title: Two weeks of night work at Oak–VGH
summary: The November 3 notice listed overnight shifts starting November 2 to finish connecting the water main. Nearby residents and businesses were to receive notice of water shutoffs.

title: Temporary supports to come down at Clayton Station
summary: Crews scheduled an extended shift on November 11 to remove supports from the station’s finished concrete sections.

title: Tile and ceilings go in at Great Northern Way–Emily Carr
summary: Inside the station, crews were laying tile, fitting ceilings and building masonry walls. Above them, workers still had to waterproof and cover the roof.

title: Early concrete pour at Bakerview–166 Street
summary: Work was set to start at 4:30 a.m. on November 9 so crews could pour the concrete in one go. The shift could run until 10 p.m.

title: Surrey council makes SkyTrain to Newton a priority
summary: On November 9, council directed staff to pursue an Expo Line extension along King George Boulevard. Construction funding remained undecided.

title: Five nights of water-main work near Broadway–City Hall
summary: Starting November 19, crews planned to connect businesses on the north side of Broadway between Cambie and Yukon to the permanent main. Water shutoffs were scheduled overnight.

title: Track work to close part of Industrial Avenue
summary: Crews scheduled concrete and track work on the elevated line for November 24. Industrial Avenue was due to close from 201A Street to 203 Street between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m.

title: Wider sidewalks planned at Broadway–City Hall
summary: Crews plan to start November 23 on the north side of Broadway between Alberta and Yukon, then move to the south side. Pedestrians will follow detours while the sidewalks are rebuilt into 2027.

title: Premier renews promise to extend SkyTrain to Newton
summary: Premier Lorne Doerkson cited the extension when he named Surrey-Newton MLA Harj Dhaliwal parliamentary secretary for TransLink. He gave no construction budget or start date.

title: Fleetwood Flyer finishes its stretch east of 152 Street
summary: With that section of elevated trackway in place, crews prepared to take the lifting gantry apart. A revised notice set turn restrictions at 152 Street for November 16 to December 19.

title: Sunday beam lifts added on Fraser Highway
summary: From November 12 to December 12, only local traffic could use Fraser Highway between Whalley Boulevard and 140 Street while crews lifted beams into place.

title: Crews set dates to dismantle the Fleetwood Flyer
summary: Work east of 152 Street was scheduled from 6 p.m. November 26 to 6 a.m. November 30. Fraser Highway would carry eastbound traffic only during the work.

title: Access to 158 and 159 streets to close for guideway work
summary: Crews need room north of Fraser Highway to work on the guideway and install utilities for future traffic signals. Access restrictions are scheduled for November 23 and 24 and December 7 to 10.

title: Daytime closures at 68 Avenue and Fraser Highway
summary: Crews plan to rebuild the road on November 23 and December 3. Access to 68 Avenue north of Fraser Highway will close from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. both days.

title: 29th Avenue elevator to close for about four months
summary: TransLink scheduled the replacement for September 29. An accessible shuttle would run between 29th Avenue and Joyce–Collingwood on weekday mornings and afternoons.

title: Patterson Station gets a larger elevator
summary: TransLink planned to close the old elevator on November 3 and open its replacement in spring 2027. Riders who need step-free access would have to use another route during the work.

title: Overnight train tests planned on the Expo and Millennium lines
summary: Starting October 3, trains would run after the last passenger service to test the new control centre. TransLink expected testing to take about five months.

title: Early closures at Oakridge–41st Avenue
summary: TransLink scheduled 11 p.m. closures on selected nights from August 24 to September 22. Crews needed the time to pour concrete, fit glass panels and install a security barrier at the entrance.

title: A footpath along Thornton Street beside Great Northern Way–Emily Carr
summary: CityHallWatch photographed a pedestrian path on the west side of Thornton Street between East 1st and East 2nd avenues. The route runs beside the fenced subway construction site.

title: Regional mayors press for long-term transit funding
summary: TransLink CEO Kevin Quinn told the Mayors’ Council that existing funding would keep current service running through 2027. Radio-Canada’s account of the meeting identified the proposed UBC and Newton extensions among the projects that would need provincial support.

title: Correction: the Langley Launcher was heading toward Willowbrook
summary: The atlas entry for September 21 placed the gantry at Langley City Centre Station. B.C. described the machine moving into Langley to build the guideway over Willowbrook Drive, with Willowbrook Station still ahead.

title: Main Street utility repairs near Mount Pleasant Station
summary: Broadway Subway crews planned to adjust a manhole and resurface the road at Main Street and East 8th Avenue from November 3 to 13. The notice said homes and businesses would stay accessible.

title: Bowinn Ma backs SkyTrain across Burrard Inlet
summary: North Vancouver-Lonsdale MLA Bowinn Ma called for SkyTrain as the long-term crossing in a November 19 statement. She did not name a route or station. The regional partners are still studying which technology to use.

title: Cleaning contractor to change on the Expo and Millennium lines
summary: TransLink confirmed it would replace Dexterra, which cleans the trains, stations and maintenance facilities on both lines. The cleaners’ union said December 17 would be Dexterra’s last day.

title: Industrial Avenue track work moves to November 26
summary: Crews rescheduled the concrete pour and track installation from Tuesday to Thursday. Drivers won’t be able to reach 203 Street from Industrial Avenue from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.; alternating traffic will keep homes and businesses accessible.

title: Overnight guideway work limits turns at Highway 15 and Fraser Highway
summary: From 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., crews will close the right turn from northbound Highway 15 onto Fraser Highway from November 26 to December 1. The restriction shifts to the right turn from eastbound Fraser Highway onto southbound Highway 15 on December 2 and 3.

title: Langley Launcher moves east from Willowbrook
summary: The Aldergrove Star reported that the gantry building the elevated guideway had moved east from the Willowbrook Station site. It had less than 1.5 kilometres to go before reaching the end of the line.

title: TransLink CEO leaves UBC extension timing to the province
summary: At the Board of Trade on November 20, Kevin Quinn said extending the Millennium Line from Arbutus to UBC remained a regional priority. B.C. leads the design work and has yet to publish the business case or its cost estimate.

title: Late-night track maintenance on the Richmond branch
summary: The November 15 service bulletin listed single-track service between Bridgeport and Richmond–Brighouse that Sunday. Trains in both directions were scheduled to share one track from 11 p.m. until the last train.

title: Platform 2 for both directions at Royal Oak and Edmonds
summary: TransLink scheduled track maintenance from 9:30 p.m. to the last train on November 24, 25 and 26. Trains in both directions use Platform 2 at both stations during the work. Trips through Royal Oak can take about 15 minutes longer.

title: Three nights of single-track service between Bridgeport and Richmond–Brighouse
summary: TransLink scheduled trains to share one track from 11 p.m. to the end of service on November 24, 25 and 26. Trains on the Richmond branch were scheduled to run every 20 minutes, with last trains leaving about five minutes later than usual.

title: B.C. directs its transportation minister to advance SkyTrain to Newton
summary: Premier Lorne Doerkson asked Transportation Minister Trevor Halford to work with Surrey, TransLink and the federal government on the extension. The letter gives no construction budget or start date.

title: November 26 track work on Industrial Avenue postponed
summary: Crews postponed the concrete pour and track installation that would have closed access to 203 Street on Thursday. The project office has yet to set a new date.

title: New hours for taking down the Fleetwood Flyer
summary: Crews scheduled overnight disassembly east of 152 Street from 10 p.m. November 25 to 7 a.m. December 2. Fraser Highway will carry eastbound through traffic only from 152 Street to 88 Avenue, first from 10 p.m. Thursday to 5 a.m. Friday, then from 10 p.m. Friday to 5 a.m. Monday, November 30.

title: Langley Launcher guideway work to close Highway 10 overnight
summary: Crews scheduled overnight guideway work east of Willowbrook from November 28 to December 11. Highway 10 between Fraser Highway and 200 Street will narrow to one lane each way at night starting December 2, with full closures from midnight to 4 a.m. during the December 8 to 11 work window.

title: TransLink readies four de-icing trains for winter
summary: Four trains are ready to spray de-icer on the power rails. Platform crews have 77 hockey sticks to clear ice and snow from train doors, and trains may run overnight to keep snow off the guideway.

title: Platform 1 at Waterfront, Burrard and Granville during weekend rail work
summary: Expo Line trains will use platform 1 at all three stations from the start of service to 10:15 a.m. on November 28 and 29, and again after 9:30 p.m. Sunday until the last train. Crews are replacing rail between Waterfront and Stadium–Chinatown. TransLink advises allowing 20 extra minutes for trips through downtown.

title: East entrance elevator maintenance at Inlet Centre
summary: The elevator from the east entrance to the VCC–Clark-bound platform was due to close for maintenance at 8 a.m. Thursday, November 26. TransLink scheduled the work through 4 p.m. Friday, November 27.

title: Four days of escalator work at Renfrew
summary: TransLink scheduled maintenance on the up escalator between the Compass ticket machines and the VCC–Clark-bound platform, from 8 a.m. November 24 to 4 p.m. November 27.
